subject.title: Feature: Pre-compaction agent notification, structured handoff window, and deferral mechanism

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class pre-threshold compaction warnings, a structured handoff/checkpoint turn, and bounded agent-requested compaction deferral to core, or keep the current memoryFlush, notifyUser, hook, and checkpoint model as the supported lifecycle?
rationale: The request changes compaction timing, persisted session semantics, public config, workspace-write timing, and authority handling across compaction boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the product and security contract.

options.title: Design Core Lifecycle
options.body: Define warning thresholds, handoff checkpoint schema, deferral authorization, audit, timeout, and upgrade rules before implementation.

options.title: Narrow To Notices Only
options.body: Limit core work to user/agent-visible warning improvements and leave deferral and checkpoint authority out of scope for now.

options.title: Decline New Core Surface
options.body: Keep existing memoryFlush, compaction hooks, notifyUser, and checkpoint metadata as the supported model and close narrower follow-ups accordingly.

recommendation.title: Design Core Lifecycle
recommendation.body: Define warning thresholds, handoff checkpoint schema, deferral authorization, audit, timeout, and upgrade rules before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest available routing candidate because he introduced pre-compaction memoryFlush and has adjacent memory/compaction history.
